answer: Stake-weighted sortition defeats Sybil splitting: each epoch a verifiable random beacon, an unsteerable river of entropy, samples a committee with probability proportional to one custody-bonded stake. Split that fixed stake across a hundred clones and each is a stranded island carrying its own minimum bond, yet their summed selection probability stays identical, so extra identities are pure deadweight. Any two clones seated together that sign conflicting votes expose a shared key and are slashed, leaving the swarm on shale: more bonds, zero added influence, standing equivocation risk.
